title: Not with Our Mortal Eyes
description: Not with Our Mortal Eyes in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 108, headed “Christ unseen and beloved, 1 Pet. 1. 8”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Not with our mor-tal eyes Have we be-held the Lord, Yet we re-joice to hear his Name, And love him in his word.

lines: Yet we rejoice to hear his Name,
And love him in his word.
On earth we want the sight
Yet, Lord, our inmost thoughts delight
And when we taste thy love,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
